newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Asia Terminals Ltd closes HK$1.75 bln loan.
newsitem.headline: Asia Terminals Ltd closes HK$1.75 bln loan.

text.p: Asia Terminals Ltd's HK$1.75 billion loan facility has been allotted, arrangers ABN Amro and Societe Generale Asia said.
The facility has a final maturity of seven years. Repayment is in 27 semi-equal annual instalments commencing six months after the agreement date.
It pays an interest margin of 60 basis points over the Hong Kong Interbank Offered Rate. Management fees are 26 basis points for arrangers and 20 basis points for managers.
The deal is secured by mortgage over building, floating charge over the borrower's assets, assignment of insurances, assignment of income, and charge of operating and retention account.

Financial covenants of the loan state that the company's net worth must be above HK$700 million, that it must maintain debt service coverage of 1.15 times and that its dividend payout must not exceed 50 percent of net profit
Coordinating arrangers are ABN Amro Bank and Societe Generale Asia.
Arrangers are Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi, BNP Hong Kong, Commerz East Asia, Long Term Credit Bank of Japan, Sakura Bank, Sanwa Bank, Standard Chartered Bank and WestLB.

Lead managers are Bank Austria, Bank Brussels Lambert Hong Kong, Bank Indosuez/Carr Indosuez Asia, Dai-ichi Kangyo Bnk, Fuji Bank Hong Kong, Industrial Bank of Japan Hong Kong, Tokai Bank Hong Kong, Wing Lung Bank, DG Bank, DBS, and Yasuda Trust and Banking Co.
Asia Terminals is largely held by New World Infrastructure Ltd.
